title: World War II foo fighters

tellings.quote: it would be good to get explanations of the Foo Fighters during World War II, the pilots that saw these things.
And they were simply balls of light that rose up out of the countryside that appeared to have some kind of intelligent control,
tellings.difference: Told by Nick Cook, who places them over Germany and describes balls of light rising from the countryside, apparently under intelligent control.
tellings.link_reason: These are the same World War II foo fighters, the balls of light seen by wartime pilots.

tellings.quote: During World War II, the Foo Fighters were commonly spotted, and there were all sorts of radar beams flying around. They never reported any crashes then.
tellings.difference: Adds that the foo fighters flew through many radar beams and none were reported to crash, offered as an argument against the radar-crash theory.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about the WWII foo fighters seen across the war theatres in general.

as_told.title: WWII foo fighters flew through radar beams with no crashes

plain: During World War II, pilots reported strange lights or objects following their planes, which came to be called foo fighters. Michael Shermer, a researcher known as a skeptic, says during a debate on Jesse Michels' podcast that it would be good to get explanations for what those pilots saw, since unexplained cases like these come up whenever people argue about UFOs.
